astir:refresh-matrix.name: Rapid Recycler
astir:refresh-matrix.description:
This Astir's Drone Bay runs on a tighter, more efficient cycle, letting each Drone re-arm faster than most.

Your Drones gain the Blitz tag, and lose the Limited tag if they carry it (today, only Attack Drone does).

astir-part:extra-arms.name: Additional Arms
astir-part:extra-arms.description:
Bolting a second set of arms onto a chassis is easy. Wiring them into the pilot's own reflexes without them fighting each other is the hard part.

Two extra arms and hands.

astir-part:divination-codex.name: Tactical Databank
astir-part:divination-codex.description:
A constantly-updated archive of enemy doctrine, terrain surveys and battlefield telemetry, cross-referenced and served up to a networked pilot in a heartbeat.

Ask 1 question from the Read the Room list.

astir-part:flourish-component.name: Backup Capacitor Bank
astir-part:flourish-component.description:
Where a standard reactor relies on one clean power curve, this rig keeps a second bank charged in reserve, ready to catch the surplus the instant the main line spikes past spec.

Regain 1 Power when you roll doubles (once per roll).

astir-part:familiar-matrix.name: Drone Bay
astir-part:familiar-matrix.description:
A dedicated bay and datalink rig lets one pilot store, launch and coordinate a full flight of remote units without splitting their attention.

Holds and comes with one set of Drones of your choice.

astir-part:alchemical-suite.name: Combat Stimilation Suite
astir-part:alchemical-suite.description:
A rack of preformulated aerosol canisters, vented directly into the cockpit's HVAC system on demand.

  • Red: Remove a peril related to physical injury or wounds. Metallic aftertaste.
  • Blue: Take advantage when you next weave magic. Sharp and clean.
  • Yellow: Take a risk. Act with confidence when you next exchange blows or strike decisively. Bitter, with a kick.

Take 1 of each Stim when someone leads a Sortie.

astir-part:chameleon-cloak.name: Optical Camouflage
astir-part:chameleon-cloak.description:
They can't hit what they can't see.

Trigger the optical camouflage field for a Scene. The next risk you take is 'revealed'.

astir-part:resistance-charms.name: Specialized System Hardening
astir-part:resistance-charms.description:
While it's difficult to offer broad protection against every kind of damage, more specific hazards are relatively simple to harden an Astir against.

Examples:

  • Redundant Actuators (lowers dangers from limb loss). Crawl. Climb. Rip. Tear. Many hands make light work.
  • Failsafe Relays (lowers dangers from comms disruption). Hear you loud and clear, 9th. Everyone else went quiet.
  • Grounded Conduits (lowers dangers from electricity). Don't be the fool caught out in a storm. Plan ahead.

Lowers dangers from one chosen source: Peril becomes a Risk, Risk becomes Nothing.

astir-part:heat-condensers.name: Advanced Cooling System
astir-part:heat-condensers.description:
Stopping to vent heat mid-fight can make you a sitting duck—it makes sense then that many pilots who'd rather not risk it invest in specialized coolant radiators.

Untick 'overheating' from your Astir.

ardent-feature:armour-plating.name: Composite Hull Plating
ardent-feature:armour-plating.description:
Layered composite plating bolted directly onto the frame, thick enough to matter without slowing the Ardent down too badly.

You may use this once per Sortie to reduce an incoming source of harm from a peril to a risk, or from a risk to nothing (+ward).

ardent-feature:chromatic-reserves.name: Modular Loadout Bay
ardent-feature:chromatic-reserves.description:
A bank of swappable subsystem modules lets this Ardent's crew reconfigure its combat doctrine on the fly.

Swap to any other Approach for a single Scene. Usable up to 3 times per Sortie.

astir-fists.name: Reinforced Fists
astir-fists.description: Every Astir can fall back on its reinforced fists, but they don't make for graceful brawlers. Also seen as Concealed Vibro-Blades, Close-Range Chainguns, or a Mining Drill.

forceknife.name: Vibroblade
forceknife.description: Short (for an Astir) blades fitted with a high-frequency vibro-edge, vibroblades are good for when you find yourself up close and personal. Also seen as a Throwing Glaive, Charged Hatchet, or Serrated Combat Knives.

force-repeater.name: Auxiliary Machine Gun
force-repeater.description: A fully automatic, large caliber machine gun firing kinetic rounds, serving as an effective reserve weapon. Also seen as a Sidearm, Mining Laser, or Point-Defense Turret.

rayrifle.name: Beam Rifle
rayrifle.description: Beam rifles are the workhorse of most armies when it comes to arming Astirs. A highly efficient capacitor cycle means every shot draws an almost meaningless amount of reactor power. Also seen as a Service Rifle, Arc Cannon, or Recycler Rifle.

titan-bow.name: Laser Cannon
titan-bow.description: Immense, heavily-reinforced laser cannons, taller than even some Astirs. While some baulk at taking a bulky single-shot weapon into the field, others point to the ability to punch a hole through Carrier hulls as a valuable upside. Also seen as a Single-Shot Railgun, Beam Sniper, or Anti-Materiel Rifle.

warp-slinger.name: Gatling Turret
warp-slinger.description: A gun incorporating multiple linked barrels and a simple firing mechanism that can be triggered by even an untrained gunner. Also seen as an MG Turret, Point-Defense Laser, or a Rotary Cannon.

seeker-cluster.name: Guided Missile Pod
seeker-cluster.description: Guided by a simple onboard targeting computer, this pod launches a swarm of small guided munitions to hound a particular target. Though they struggle to pierce armour, these warheads shatter on impact, scattering sharp shrapnel. Also seen flechette guns, Shock Rod Launcher, or Micro-missiles.

forceblade.name: Beam Saber
forceblade.description: Your typical, garden-variety sword made out of a projected energy blade. It cuts well and won't explode - what else do you want? Also seen as a Thermal Cutter or a Pneumatic Hammer.

blazewands.name: Grenade Launcher Racks
blazewands.description: Arranged in paired racks and loaded with incendiary charges, short-range launchers are a common and potent weapon when it comes to arming Astirs. Also seen as Acid Pods or a Plasma Mortar.

novawhip.name: Nanite Whip
novawhip.description: A flexible, extendable weapon made from hardware-degrading nanomaterials. Also seen as a Plasma Cable or a Storm Gauntlet.

overcharged-bolts.name: Gauss Cannon
overcharged-bolts.description: If you need something punchier, you can take perfectly standard Astir hardware—a basic railgun, for example—and simply feed it far, far more reactor power than expected. Also seen as an Ion Cannon, Gauss Rifle, or an Overcharged Railgun.

chaos-revolver.name: Fusion Pistol
chaos-revolver.description: A thick, metal sidearm with a revolver-style grip. The rotating chambers are loaded with unstable fusion cells, and their output is immense (and volatile). Also seen as an Acid Thrower or a Phase Disruptor Cannon.

wisp-familiar.name: Attack Drone
wisp-familiar.description: Attack drones are by far the most common remote combat unit, and for most pilots are the default choice. Small hovering constructs that pack a surprising punch for their size, they're limited by their short battery life. Also seen as an Assault Funnel Launcher, Incendiary Charges, or a Swarm of Micro-Drones. Drone — requires a Drone Control Bay Astir Part; rolls +CHANNEL for Exchange Blows and Strike Decisively; perils from its loss clear automatically during Downtime.

mote-familiar.name: Blast Drone
mote-familiar.description: Blast drones are small guided munitions carrying a volatile incendiary charge, detonating in a fiery blast the instant they strike a target. Pilots use them sparingly — a hit can set off every other blast drone in the area in a chain detonation. Also seen as a Remote Bomb, Volatile Munition, or Frag Pod. Drone — requires a Drone Control Bay Astir Part; rolls +CHANNEL for Exchange Blows and Strike Decisively; perils from its loss clear automatically during Downtime.

needle-familiar.name: Restraint Drone
needle-familiar.description: Restraint drones pin their targets in place with thin, hardened steel spikes. While lacking when it comes to decisive blows, they excel at restraining and harassing foes. Also seen as a Glue Turret, Labour Drones, or a Netting Launcher. Drone — requires a Drone Control Bay Astir Part; rolls +CHANNEL for Exchange Blows and Strike Decisively; perils from its loss clear automatically during Downtime.

claw-familiar.name: Crow Drone
claw-familiar.description: Sharp-clawed constructs of servo-driven metal and composite plating.  Winged and black, their silhouettes earned them the 'Crow Drone' moniker. Also seen as Hunter-Killer Units, Phantom Drones, or Saw Drones. Drone — requires a Drone Control Bay Astir Part; rolls +CHANNEL for Exchange Blows and Strike Decisively; perils from its loss clear automatically during Downtime.

ardent-feature:bolt-sigils.name: EMP Edge
ardent-feature:bolt-sigils.description: A capacitor-lined blade, primed to discharge a disabling electromagnetic pulse on impact.

ardent-feature:brimstone-pods.name: Incendiary Pods
ardent-feature:brimstone-pods.description: Pods of volatile incendiary charges, lobbed to cover a wide area — better rationed than relied on.

hewer.name: Plasma Saw
hewer.description: A circular saw, spun at blistering speeds by a superheated plasma injector fed by compressed coolant from the deep heart of Repose.

colossus-repeater.name: Autocannon Repeater
colossus-repeater.description: Using a sophisticated autoloader, Autocannon Repeaters fire armour-piercing rounds for maximum penetration. In a pinch, a talented pilot can work the reloading mechanism quickly enough for multiple follow-up shots.

infantry-weapon-i.name: Infantry Sidearm
infantry-weapon-i.description: Simple, sturdy gear like sidearms and combat knives.

greatsword-i.name: Heavy Vibroblade
greatsword-i.description: A large, motor-assisted blade with good reach and weight, perfect for taking heads.

enchanted-blade-i.name: Charged Blade
enchanted-blade-i.description: What was once simple steel now carries a live electrical charge, thanks to an integrated capacitor.

bow-i.name: Assault Rifle
bow-i.description: For when you don't need anything fancy, a standard-issue assault rifle is perfectly capable of doing the job for as long as you have ammunition.

raypistol-i.name: Laser Pistol
raypistol-i.description: A powerful but short-lived laser sidearm, fitted with a comfortable grip.

rayrifle-i.name: Laser Rifle
rayrifle-i.description: A heavy rifle, often using charged battery cells for a single devastating shot. Their bulk, heavy recoil and cost makes them highly uncommon, but not overly so: after all, little else hand-held will put a hole through an Astir.

construct-sensor-i.name: Tactical Sensor Table
construct-sensor-i.description: Circular tables fitted with a surface of servo-driven sensor pins. The pins independently rise and fall when unregistered Constructs are detected within a certain radius, building a rough three-dimensional relief of oncoming forces. The height of raised pins corresponds to the size of a detected Construct, and larger tables with denser arrays allow for more precise reliefs.

grappling-hook-i.name: Grapnel Launcher
grappling-hook-i.description: Allows you to climb or grapple. A small sturdy grip attached to a barrel loaded with a steel hook or magnetic grip, propelled by a compressed-gas charge. An attached cable can then be reeled in, allowing the holder to quickly relocate.

arcane-charge-i.name: Demolition Charge
arcane-charge-i.description: A shaped explosive charge on a timer fuse. Stick it on an Astir, light the fuse, and run for your life.

bloodletter-i.name: Pig Sticker
bloodletter-i.description: The rank-and-file of the Faces Of Progress carry these sinister spears, engineered specifically to punch through armour plating and flesh alike.

little-shark-ii.name: Cryo Harpoon
little-shark-ii.description: When the first mariner's ardent team was dispatched to interfere with Progress reinforcements, they found their equipment lacking for undersea use. Dubbed Cryo Harpoons, these ardent-fit launchers stacked with short-range cryogenic charges provided an easy way of ruining ship hulls. Descriptive tags: Freezing.

colour-spray-i.name: Dye Canister
colour-spray-i.description: A staple of any academy prankster: small pressurized canisters, full of industrial dye that marks any surface it touches in gaudy colour. It washes off… after a few days.

wayward-skull-i.name: Salvaged AI Core
wayward-skull-i.description: Derelict AI cores are easier to find than ever in the wreckage fields of the Kessler Drift, and are often a great source of information and advice. Recover one, and all the newest rumours will find your ear. Descriptive tags: Sturdy, Chattering, Autonomous.

bestiary-array-ii.name: Holoprojector Array
bestiary-array-ii.description: A popular weapon among the Hollow Ranks, the Holoprojector Array casts flickering holographic decoys shaped like beasts of war, hard to pin down and irritatingly effective at scrambling Astir targeting systems.
